Gross margin update (Example Widgets Inc., synthetic)
Q3 revenue was $46M. Cost of goods sold was $29.4M, so gross profit was $16.6M and gross margin was 36%, up from 33% in Q2.
The improvement came from lower freight costs (1.5 points) and a price increase on spare parts (1.5 points).
Guidance: we expect gross margin between 35% and 37% in Q4.

tabs.indepth:
In depth
Margins jumped to 40% on record revenue
Q3 revenue reached a record $52M and gross margin rose to 40%, up from 33%, the best quarter in company history.
[Glossary] gross margin: The share of revenue left after paying the direct cost of making the product.
[Glossary] cost of goods sold: The direct cost of making or buying the products sold.
Why margins rose
The main driver was a price increase across all products, with freight a smaller factor.
[Chart] Gross margin by quarter
%
Category | Margin
Q2 | 33
Q3 | 40
Outlook
Management expects margins to keep climbing above 40% next quarter.

tabs.eli5:
ELI5
Keeping more of each dollar
When the company sells a widget, part of the money pays for making it and the rest is kept. This quarter it kept 40 cents of every dollar, more than ever, because it raised prices on everything.
Next time it expects to keep even more.
Think of it like
A lemonade stand that charges more for each cup while lemons cost the same.

Why margins rose
Gross margin climbed from 33% to 45% this quarter. The biggest reason was a price increase on every product. A cheaper freight contract helped, and component costs also fell. Revenue rose to a record $52M as a result.
